s1.reference: Assessment of a fifty-two-year-old male with three days of fever, productive cough, chest discomfort, breathlessness, fatigue and reduced appetite. Denies vomiting and wheezing; no known drug allergy. Past history of hypertension and type two diabetes; provisional diagnosis community-acquired pneumonia. Examination: temperature one hundred and one degrees Fahrenheit, blood pressure one hundred and thirty over eighty-five millimetres of mercury, pulse ninety-two beats per minute, respiratory rate twenty-two, saturation ninety-four percent on room air. Investigations: complete blood count and chest X-ray. Plan: paracetamol six hundred and fifty milligrams thrice daily, amoxicillin with clavulanic acid as advised, glucose monitoring. Diet: light home diet, warm fluids, dal-rice, adequate water. General: complete antibiotics, daily temperature check, return for worsening breathlessness or high fever. Follow up in three days.

s2.reference: Dictation for a forty-eight-year-old female with five days of headache, dizziness, blurred vision and evening tiredness. Denies chest pain and breathlessness; no known drug allergy. Past history hypertension and high cholesterol; diagnosis uncontrolled essential hypertension. Examination: blood pressure one fifty over ninety-five millimetres of mercury, pulse eighty-six beats per minute, temperature ninety-eight point six degrees Fahrenheit, saturation ninety-eight percent on room air. Investigations: kidney function and ECG. Plan: continue amlodipine five milligrams once daily, home BP charting. Diet: low salt, no pickles or processed food, vegetables, two litres water daily. General: morning BP check, daily walk, emergency review for severe headache, chest pain or vision change. Follow up in one week.

s3.reference: Sixty-year-old male with sudden right arm-leg weakness, slurred speech and facial droop one hour ago, conscious and answering. Denies fever, seizure and head injury; no known drug allergy. Past history hypertension and type two diabetes; provisional diagnosis acute ischemic stroke. Examination: blood pressure one sixty over ninety millimetres of mercury, pulse eighty-eight beats per minute, saturation ninety-seven percent on room air, right-sided weakness with facial droop. Investigations: urgent CT brain and blood glucose. Plan: stroke-unit monitoring, nil by mouth until swallow review, onset-time documentation. Diet: nil by mouth, then soft diet after swallow test only. General: watch consciousness and weakness, alert team at once for worsening. No food or aspirin until reviewed.

s4.reference: Fifty-eight-year-old male smoker with thirty minutes of heavy central chest pressure radiating to the left arm, breathlessness and sweating. Denies fever and cough; no known drug allergy. Past history hypertension and high cholesterol; provisional diagnosis acute coronary syndrome. Examination: blood pressure one forty-five over ninety millimetres of mercury, pulse ninety-six beats per minute, respiratory rate twenty, saturation ninety-five percent on room air. Investigations: ECG and troponin. Plan: aspirin as advised, continuous rhythm and BP monitoring. Diet: light low salt low fat diet, no smoking or alcohol. General: complete bed rest, report worsening pain, sweating, breathlessness or fainting at once. Follow up in cardiology in two days.

drugs.quote: Plan: aspirin as advised, continuous rhythm and BP monitoring.

s5.reference: Young adult female started on amoxicillin today for throat infection, with whole-body itching twenty minutes later, rash on arms-neck and mild lip swelling with throat tightness, still talking normally. Denies prior penicillin allergy and wheezing. No past major illness; diagnosis acute allergic reaction, suspected amoxicillin allergy. Examination: saturation ninety-six percent, pulse one hundred and eight beats per minute, blood pressure one ten over seventy millimetres of mercury. Plan: stop amoxicillin, antihistamines ready, adrenaline if anaphylaxis, document allergy. Diet: light home food, plenty of fluids. General: watch for wheeze, swelling or BP fall; never repeat amoxicillin without advice. Return if throat tightens. Follow up tomorrow.

s6.reference: Elderly diabetic father took morning insulin but skipped breakfast, then sweating, shakiness, dizziness and confusion within one hour, conscious and swallowing. Denies vomiting and fever; no known drug allergy. Past history type two diabetes on insulin and metformin; diagnosis hypoglycaemia from missed meal. Examination: glucose fifty-four milligrams per decilitre, rising to seventy-two after sweet drink. Plan: fast sugar now, recheck every fifteen to thirty minutes, hold extra insulin until review. Diet: never skip meals after insulin; dal, rice, roti on time plus bedtime snack. General: carry sugar always, monitor twenty-four hours, rush for unconsciousness, seizure or repeat lows. Follow up in two days.
